title: Unknown stage names escape the validation boundary as raw ValueError exceptions
observed_behavior: Both exported stage-boundary helpers normalize Pydantic ValidationError into ValidationFailure, but an unknown stage string is rejected by StageName conversion as a bare ValueError. Isolated probes showed validate_stage_payload('bogus', {}) and validate_stage_result('bogus', a structurally valid failed StageResult) each raise ValueError with no structured details.
expected_invariant: Public validation-boundary helpers should convert every invalid caller-supplied stage or payload/result shape into the documented ValidationFailure type with stable structured details, so callers do not need exception-type knowledge from lower contract layers.
root_cause: validate_stage_payload catches only pydantic.ValidationError around build_stage_request, and validate_stage_result catches only pydantic.ValidationError around StageName(stage); enum conversion raises built-in ValueError before either helper can normalize it.
failure_scenario: A future runtime caller that catches ValidationFailure for operator-visible contract errors can instead receive an unexpected raw ValueError for an invalid or stale stage name, bypassing the intended structured error path and potentially surfacing as a generic command/API failure.
evidence: Complete source read: boundary.py lines 68-72 and 75-88 catch only ValidationError while contracts/stages.py converts with StageName(stage).
Isolated current-HEAD payload probe returned ValueError, 'bogus' is not a valid StageName, details=None.
Isolated current-HEAD result probe used make_stage_result to construct a fully valid failed unknown-stage result and returned the same raw ValueError with no details.

The focused validation/API suites passed (52 tests plus 376 subtests), but repository search found no negative test for unknown stage names and no current production caller of the stage helpers outside contract tests.
affected_flows: future orchestration callers relying on ValidationFailure
operator-facing normalization of stale or invalid stage identifiers
existing_safeguards: Known-stage malformed payloads/results are normalized from Pydantic ValidationError, StageResult shape validation is strict, and active Local API payload validation has its own broader TypeError/ValueError normalization.
safeguard_gap: Enum/registry conversion failures in the two stage helpers are outside the caught exception set, and no regression test asserts their public exception contract for unknown stages.
tests_missing: Unknown-stage validate_stage_payload returns ValidationFailure with details
Unknown-stage structurally valid validate_stage_result returns ValidationFailure with details
Caller-level assertion that all invalid stage boundary inputs share one exception contract
recommended_remediation: Catch ValueError (and any intentional registry KeyError if reachable) at both stage-helper boundaries and wrap it in ValidationFailure using a stable prefix/details shape; add focused unknown-stage regression tests.
remediation_risk: low: exception normalization changes only invalid-input behavior, but callers that currently depend on bare ValueError should be checked
validation_rung: Focused stage-contract and boundary unit tests, API command contract tests, py_compile, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current operational-contract finding; prior line review did not probe unknown enum conversion at this boundary.
